transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Basically, what brings me in is that I feel like I’m just constantly running on a motor lately. It’s... well, the second I finish one thing, whether I'm at school teaching or back at home, I just immediately jump right into the next thing. I never seem to be able to just shut myself off.
Lately, have you been needing less sleep than usual and still feeling rested?

No, I wouldn't say that. I definitely still need my sleep. I mean, I might be going non-stop all day long, but if I don't get a normal amount of sleep at night, I'm definitely tired the next day. I don't wake up feeling rested if I've only had a few hours, if that's what you mean.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

No, I wouldn't say I'm much of a worrier. I mean, sure, my job can be stressful sometimes—teaching special ed definitely has its moments—but I don't find myself getting anxious or worrying when there isn't a clear reason for it. So, no, that's not really an issue for me.
Have you been this way since you were a child?

Yes, absolutely. My mother actually used to joke that even back in elementary school, I basically taught the class from my seat. I was just always out of my chair, talking, or... well, cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, yeah, this has been a part of who I am long before adulthood. It's definitely not something that just started recently with any family changes or anything like that.
